title: Architecture review: KV cache splitter — performance tradeoffs (2026-07-06)
content:
Meeting: Architecture review — KV cache splitter performance tradeoffs
Date: 2026-07-06
Attendees: Avery Chen (owner), Ravi Patel, Maya Thompson, Diego Alvarez, Linnea Borg, + notes from on-call (Slack thread #kv-cache-splitter)

Agenda:
- Quick recap of the splitter RFC (goal, constraints)
- Present recent microbenchmarks and latency/cost curves
- Discuss eviction/retention impact when splitting across routes
- Decision points: eager vs lazy split, routing policy, metrics to surface
- Action items and next steps

Recap (2 min):
- Splitter purpose: reduce per-request KV contention by routing prefixes & KV slices to different cache shards (logical split by route/model/tenant affinity). Goal is lower tail latency on hot prefixes while preserving cache hit-rate for prompter workloads. See RFC: CONFLUENCE-4567.

Benchmarks presented (Maya):
- Test harness: synthetic trace, 2M requests, 24-hour hot-spot window, backend LRU baseline vs splitter variants.
- Key metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency (ms), tokens/sec, cache hit-rate, GPU utilization, additional RPC overhead.
- Results (summary):
  * Baseline (no-split): p99 generation latency 284ms, cache hit-rate 63%
  * Splitter eager (pre-allocate per-route slice): p99 210ms (-26%), hit-rate 59% (slight drop), RPC overhead +6%
  * Splitter lazy (on-demand slice creation + prefetch): p99 238ms (-16%), hit-rate 62%, RPC overhead +3%
  * Splitter + adaptive retention (hot-only retention): p99 198ms (-30%), hit-rate 60%, extra mem overhead +8%
- Notes: eager split has best tail but increases cross-shard eviction for warm-but-not-hot prefixes. Adaptive retention reduces evictions but requires more frequent hotness detection signals.

Discussion highlights:
- Ravi: latency improvements are convincing for high-QPS tenants, but we must quantify memory and RPC overhead for Dedicated customers where costs are predictable.
- Diego: multi-tenant isolation concern — eager splitting can amplify tenant imbalance (hot tenant gets more slices), need fairness policy.
- Linnea: instrumentation gaps — current tracing doesn't correlate prefix -> slice mapping easily. We should add slice-id to spans before rollout.
- Maya: prefetch design needs throttling to avoid busy-wait on cold starts; proposed backoff/credit-based prefetch.

Decision consensus (agreed):
1) Default behavior: start with lazy split + prefetch (safe middle ground). Rationale: reduces unnecessary memory fragmentation and gives similar p95 improvements while preserving hit-rate.
2) Offer eager-split as opt-in per-route flag for high-QPS, latency-sensitive routes (will be behind config + rollout guard).
3) Implement adaptive retention (hot-only retention) as an incremental improvement, gated by telemetry for eviction/regrowth costs.
4) Add slice-id to tracing spans and surface slice-level metrics in Console (per-slice hit-rate, evictions, memory).

Open design items (no final decision):
- Fairness policy for multi-tenant sharing: should we cap slices per-tenant or allocate based on token-credits? (Action: Ravi to prototype cap-based policy)
- Prefetch throttling algorithm: simple token bucket vs credit-based with backoff. (Action: Maya to benchmark both)
- Persistence and recovery: how to restore slice mappings after process restart without causing flash cold start. Options: durable metadata store vs soft-rebuild. (Action: Diego to design)

Action items:
- Avery: draft updated RFC patch with lazy-split implementation plan + opt-in flag, include rollout checklist (due 2026-07-13). Linked: https://github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/456 (WIP).
- Maya: run prefetch throttling benchmarks (token-bucket vs credit-backoff) and produce numbers for p50/p95/p99 and extra RPC overhead (due 2026-07-10).
- Ravi: prototype tenant cap policy and simulate fairness tradeoffs on synthetic traces (due 2026-07-20).
- Diego: propose recovery strategy for slice mappings (durable vs soft rebuild) with failure scenarios and perf impact (due 2026-07-14).
- Linnea: implementation task to add slice-id to traces + update trace instrumentation doc (due 2026-07-09).

Risks & mitigation:
- Memory amplification: eager split can increase memory use and evictions. Mitigate by opt-in and adaptive retention. Add memory ceiling metrics per-host.
- Cost for Dedicated customers: extra RPCs and memory may increase unit cost. We will add a cost-estimation dashboard and restrict eager-split to paid cohorts initially.
- Rollout risk: flash cold start after restart — mitigate with soft rebuild and staggered restarts across pool.

Next steps / follow-up meeting:
- Triage action items in weekly sync (owner updates). Tentative follow-up architecture review in 2 weeks (2026-07-20) to review Maya/Ravi/Diego prototypes.

Notes & references:
- RFC draft: CONFLUENCE-4567 (splitter design, diagrams, alternatives)
- Jira epic: JIRA-SRV-789 (splitter project)
- GH PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/456
- Slack thread: #kv-cache-splitter (recent perf runs and raw logs)

Informal notes (from meeting):
- "eager split feels like trading memory for tail": short phrase repeated 3x.
- team agreed lazy-first reduces blast radius.
- need better synthetic traces that mimic multi-tenant diurnal patterns — current harness is too uniform.

Document history:
- created by Avery Chen 2026-07-06
- minor edits (benchmarks clarified) by Maya Thompson 2026-07-07
